findings.title: Update-time invalidation check uses org-wrapped models, so it can skip invalidation and leave the login cache stale
findings.body:
`update()` passes `idpById = getById(...)` (line 91) as `original`. `getById` returns `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...)` (lines 141, 432-446), whose `isEnabled()` is false when the linked org or the organization provider is disabled. The `updated` model usually comes from `getByAlias`/`getById` too, so it is wrapped the same way. `getLoginPredicate()` calls `isEnabled()`, so for an IDP linked to a disabled org both `test(original)` and `test(updated)` return false whatever the stored fields say. The early return at lines 405-407 then skips invalidation.

But the cached set is built from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` (lines 229/238), which is not org-enabled-aware. So:
- Org disabled, IDP X is public and cached. Admin sets `hideOnLogin=true` or `linkOnly=true` on X. No invalidation. When the org is re-enabled, `getForLogin` returns X from the stale cached id set. `getById` gives the fresh model, but `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` only re-checks `isEnabled()` (lines 75/80), so X is shown on the login page although it is hidden.
- The reverse: org disabled, admin un-hides X. The cached set does not contain X and is not invalidated, so X is missing after the org is re-enabled.

It is silent. The over-invalidation in the other direction is harmless.

Fix: evaluate the predicate on unwrapped state. For `original`, use `idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId())`, as `remove()` already does with `idpDelegate.getByAlias`. For `updated`, don't depend on the wrapper's `isEnabled()`. Or simply compare the raw fields that feed the predicate (enabled, linkOnly, hideOnLogin, organizationId, BROKER_PUBLIC). Add a test that disables the org.

findings.title: Cleanup removes the literal alias "alias", so the 21 IDPs created by the test are never removed
findings.body:
`testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` (also line 425) targets an IDP named `alias`, which does not exist. It was copied from line 303. The `idp-alias-*` IDPs are left in the realm, and the realm persists across the test methods of the class.

The test asserts absolute counts (REALM_ONLY == 5, ALL == 10, lines 404-414). Leaked login-eligible realm-level IDPs from other methods break those counts. `testCacheIDPByOrg` leaks `org-idp-*`, which become realm-level once the orgs are deleted by cleanup. Whether the test passes then depends on JUnit method order.

Use `"idp-alias-" + i` (capture the alias in a final local variable) and `"idp-alias-20"` for the cleanup.

findings.title: Bean re-checks only isEnabled; hideOnLogin/linkOnly are not re-checked against cached results
findings.body: The comment says "re-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped", and only `isEnabled()` is re-checked after `getForLogin`. Cached `getForLogin` results are id sets resolved through `getById`, so the bean now trusts cache invalidation for every other login field (hideOnLogin, linkOnly, BROKER_PUBLIC). The `onlyOrganizationBrokers` branch with an org (lines 66-68) filters all of them. Applying `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` here would make the bean robust against the stale-cache case in the finding on `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:405`. The same applies to `IdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders` (line 238), though realm-level IDPs are not org-wrapped.

contracts.action: New cached `getForLogin(mode, organizationId)` in the Infinispan IDP storage provider
contracts.equivalent_path: `getByOrganization` in the same class (lines 168-211), which caches a set of IDP ids per search key in an `IdentityProviderListQuery`, then resolves each id through `getById`.
contracts.before_after: Before: the default `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` ran the JPA queries on every login page render. After: the id set is cached under `<realm>.idp.login.<mode>` with a per-organizationId search key. The code mirrors the `getByOrganization` structure (invalid check, query miss, search-key miss, dangling-id fallback). Cached ids are resolved via `getById`, which returns org-aware wrappers.
contracts.visible_effect: Login page IDP lists (`OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`, `IdentityProviderBean`) come from the cache. The org-aware bean re-checks `isEnabled()` because wrapped models report false for a disabled org.
contracts.failure_mode: Stale list when invalidation is skipped: see the finding on lines 403-418 (org disabled while an IDP's login fields change). The dangling-id fallback re-registers invalidation and queries JPA, matching the sibling.

contracts.action: Login-cache invalidation on IDP create, update and remove
contracts.equivalent_path: `registerCountInvalidation` and `registerIDPInvalidation` in the same class. Org link/unlink goes through `JpaOrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider`, which call `session.identityProviders().update`.
contracts.before_after: Create and remove invalidate only if the IDP satisfies `getLoginPredicate()`. `remove` now always calls `idpDelegate.getByAlias` (an extra DB lookup even on a cache hit) and uses that raw model, which is correct. Update skips invalidation when login eligibility and org id are unchanged. Linking/unlinking an org changes `organizationId` and invalidates. Removing BROKER_PUBLIC on unlink also changes eligibility, so it is covered.
contracts.visible_effect: Login page lists stay correct, except in the disabled-org case in the finding.
contracts.failure_mode: Original and updated models are org-wrapped, so `isEnabled()` is false for a disabled org and the update skips invalidation (reported as a finding).

summary: The login-IDP cache mirrors the existing `getByOrganization` pattern, and the common invalidation paths are covered. That includes org link/unlink and BROKER_PUBLIC removal, since `JpaOrganizationProvider` goes through `update`. There is one real bug. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` evaluates the login predicate on org-wrapped models, whose `isEnabled()` is false when the org is disabled. An update to a disabled org's IDP can therefore skip invalidation and leave a stale cached id set. After the org is re-enabled, an IDP made hidden or link-only can still appear on the login page, because the bean re-checks only `isEnabled`. The new test also registers cleanup for the literal alias `\"alias\"`, so it leaks 21 IDPs and its absolute counts can depend on test order.
